operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: people=12, church=9, wedding=4 rows; original_values fully read, no sampling needed.
Mixed-case identifiers: People_ID, Is_Male, Church_ID, Open_Date, Continuation_of; must double-quote in generated SQL.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent refs (`church`, `people`) inside FOREIGN KEY clauses; sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim.
wedding has composite PK (Church_ID, Male_ID, Female_ID) -> composite-PK member max_l0=30 per spec 3.3.
wedding has two FKs to the SAME parent (people) via Male_ID and Female_ID; both must draw from people.People_ID final values.
All columns notnull=0 in pragma even though PKs are declared; sqlite PK implies NOT NULL only for INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, so inserts may still fail on NULL PKs.
Open_Date and Year are INT-stored years (1831..1839, 2014..2016) but declared INT -> Number fuzzer, not Date; no text-stored dates here.
Is_Male is TEXT with values 'T'/'F' (not 'true'/'false', not 0/1) -> String fuzzer, not Bool.
Continuation_of has a truncated sample 'Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Sai' (looks like a 40-char cut); string length range will be [min,max+1] over these.
Organized_by contains an en-dash-prefixed value '– Hoton'; non-ASCII must survive sqlite write/read.
No views, triggers, indexes beyond PKs; no dangling FKs; no self-references.
Country has 5 distinct over 12 rows (ties exist); Is_Male 2 distinct; church.Name 7 distinct over 9 rows (duplicates exist).
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on People_ID/Church_ID/Age/Open_Date/Year: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from INT (no args -> scale 0, so [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation) -> tiny integer ranges, implausible for IDs and years.
Number fuzzer on Open_Date/Year will produce values like -1,0,1,2, not 1800s/2010s -> FN on year-range predicates (e.g. Open_Date BETWEEN 1830 AND 1840).
String fuzzer on Name/Country/Organized_by/Continuation_of: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings length [0,20] with 0.5 contaminate -> implausible names, FN on LIKE '%Church%' style predicates.
String fuzzer on Is_Male: fresh random strings, not 'T'/'F' -> FN on Is_Male='T' predicates; also FP risk if a random string happens to equal 'T'.
String fuzzer on Country: fresh random strings, not the 5 real countries -> FN on Country='Canada' etc.

FK columns Male_ID/Female_ID/Church_ID in wedding draw from parent final values with replacement -> duplicates across rows likely, but composite PK dedup drops them, shrinking wedding below requested size.
Composite PK (Church_ID,Male_ID,Female_ID) with tiny parent cardinalities (people=12, church=9) caps distinct wedding rows at ~9*12*12=1296; requested sizes up to 2500 will be truncated by PK dedup.
Number fuzzer on Age: [-1,1] +-1/+-2 -> ages like -3..3, implausible; FN on Age>18 / Age BETWEEN 20 AND 40.
p=0.2 default and 0.3 chance of p=0 whole-instance: with p=0, Number/String always fresh (no element reuse) -> even less plausible values.
max_l0 cap (rng*30, or 30 for composite-PK member) means after ~30 fresh draws values repeat -> ties/duplicates appear, which can cause FP on DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT) queries.
No CHECK constraints, no NOT NULL in DDL -> upstream inserts almost never fail; rows_ok ~= requested size except PK/unique dedup.
